description: Hatchet engine health from its native OpenTelemetry signals: gRPC and REST RED metrics, PostgreSQL client metrics, worker and scheduler gauges, span metrics, and sampled traces.

options.content:
**Answers:** is Hatchet healthy, is work flowing, and do workers keep up?

- **Overview** holds the golden signals: traffic (tasks created), errors, latency (queue wait, run duration), and saturation (queued tasks, slot utilization).
- Rows go from workload to workers, APIs, and the database. Collapsed rows hold sampled traces and container limits.
- **Sources:** engine OTLP metrics, Hatchet's Prometheus endpoint (`job="hatchet"`: tasks, queues, workers), and Tempo traces sampled at `SERVER_OTEL_TRACE_ID_RATIO`.
- **Filters:** Service, Environment, Namespace, and Host apply to OTLP panels; Worker and Workflow to endpoint panels. Click a worker or workflow in its table to filter by it.

panels.title: Engines reporting
panels.description: Hatchet engine processes exporting OTLP metrics within Prometheus' 5-minute lookback. 0 means the engine is down or cannot reach otel-collector-agent.

panels.title: Live workers
panels.description: Workers the scheduler can assign tasks to. A worker that stops heartbeating drops out.

panels.title: Tasks created
panels.description: Tasks created in the selected range by triggers, events, schedules, and crons.

defaults.noValue: No data: needs SERVER_PROMETHEUS_ENABLED on Hatchet

panels.title: Task failure rate
panels.description: Share of finished tasks (succeeded plus failed) in the selected range that failed. Retries are counted separately.

defaults.noValue: No data: needs SERVER_PROMETHEUS_ENABLED on Hatchet

panels.title: Queue wait p95
panels.description: 95th percentile time from queued to assigned to a worker, across all workflows, in the selected range. The largest bucket is 15 s.

defaults.noValue: No tasks assigned in this time range

panels.title: Queued tasks
panels.description: Tasks waiting for a worker slot now, across all queues.

panels.title: Busiest worker
panels.description: Highest slot utilization among live workers now. Near 100% while tasks queue means that worker is the bottleneck; the Workers table shows which one.

panels.title: gRPC server errors
panels.description: Share of gRPC calls in the selected range that ended with a server-side code (UNKNOWN, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, UNIMPLEMENTED, INTERNAL, UNAVAILABLE, DATA_LOSS).

panels.title: Task throughput
panels.description: Tasks created and finished per second. Created staying above finished means the backlog grows.

defaults.noValue: No data: needs SERVER_PROMETHEUS_ENABLED on Hatchet

panels.title: Errors
panels.description: Server-side failures per second across the engine's gRPC API, REST API, and PostgreSQL client.

panels.title: Task latency
panels.description: 95th percentile queue wait (left axis) and completed-run duration (right axis) across all workflows. Run duration excludes queue time.

defaults.noValue: No tasks assigned or finished in this time range

panels.title: Task outcomes
panels.description: Finished, retried, and rescheduled tasks per second across tenants. Scheduling timed out means no worker slot freed up before the task's schedule timeout.

defaults.noValue: No data: needs SERVER_PROMETHEUS_ENABLED on Hatchet

panels.title: Run duration p95 by workflow
panels.description: 95th percentile execution time of completed runs (start to finish, excluding queue time) per workflow; a DAG counts as one run.

defaults.noValue: No runs finished in this time range

panels.title: Queued tasks by queue
panels.description: Tasks waiting for a worker slot, by queue (one queue per task action). Workers do not own queues: any live worker that registered the action can take the task. Polled every 15 s.

panels.title: Queue wait p95 by workflow
panels.description: 95th percentile time from queued to assigned to a worker, per workflow. The largest bucket is 15 s, so waits above 15 s show as 15 s.

defaults.noValue: No tasks assigned in this time range

panels.title: Workflow summary
panels.description: Per-workflow runs, failure shares, and completed-run duration over the selected range, plus queue wait and the current backlog.

panels.title: Workers
panels.description: Live workers as the scheduler sees them: running tasks (used slots), slot capacity, and utilization. Workers that stop heartbeating drop out. Hatchet exports no task durations per worker; use Workflow summary for p95 per workflow.

panels.title: Running tasks by worker
panels.description: Tasks occupying worker slots, by worker name. Workers sharing a name are summed; the Workers table splits them by ID.

panels.title: Slot utilization by worker
panels.description: Used slots as a share of each worker's slots. A worker pinned near 100% while its queues grow needs more slots or more replicas.

panels.title: Live workers
panels.description: Workers the scheduler can assign tasks to. A worker that stops heartbeating drops out.

panels.title: Running and queued tasks
panels.description: Tasks occupying worker slots next to tasks waiting for one. A queued line that keeps rising means workers cannot keep up.

panels.title: Concurrency-controlled tasks
panels.description: Tasks held by the scheduler's in-memory concurrency indexes. Running tasks occupy a concurrency slot; queued tasks wait for one. A growing queued line means concurrency limits are holding work back. Appears once a workflow uses a concurrency strategy.

panels.title: Concurrency index size
panels.description: Concurrency keys tracked by the scheduler and the index's estimated heap usage. Many distinct concurrency keys (for example one per user) raise engine memory.

panels.title: Active SDKs
panels.description: Live workers by SDK language, SDK version, runtime, and OS. Use it to track SDK upgrades across workers. OTEL gauges keep the last value of each label set until the engine restarts, so a tenant, table, or SDK that stops reporting holds its last value.

panels.title: gRPC calls by method
panels.description: gRPC calls per second by method. Dispatcher/* serves workers, WorkflowService and AdminService serve triggers and admin calls, EventsService ingests events and logs. Heartbeats are excluded; see Live workers.

panels.title: gRPC latency (unary)
panels.description: Unary gRPC call duration percentiles. Streaming RPCs are excluded. Click an exemplar point to open a trace.

panels.title: gRPC non-OK responses
panels.description: Calls per second that ended with a status other than OK, by method and code. Server codes (UNKNOWN, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, UNIMPLEMENTED, INTERNAL, UNAVAILABLE, DATA_LOSS) point at engine faults; CANCELLED and FAILED_PRECONDITION usually mean a worker disconnected or sent a stale request.

panels.title: gRPC p95 latency by method (unary)
panels.description: 95th percentile duration per unary gRPC method.

panels.title: gRPC method summary
panels.description: Per-method calls, failure shares, and latency over the selected range. Streaming RPCs show no latency because their duration is the stream lifetime.

panels.title: Requests by status class
panels.description: REST API requests per second by response status class. The API serves the Hatchet dashboard and SDK REST clients.

panels.title: REST API latency
panels.description: REST API request duration percentiles. Click an exemplar point to open a trace.

panels.title: REST route summary
panels.description: Per-route requests, error shares, and latency over the selected range.

targets.expr: 100 * (sum by (http_request_method, http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name="$service",deployment_environment_name="$environment",service_namespace=~"$namespace",host_name=~"$host",http_response_status_code=~"4.."}[$__range])) or 0 * sum by (http_request_method, http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name="$service",deployment_environment_name="$environment",service_namespace=~"$namespace",host_name=~"$host"}[$__range]))) / (sum by (http_request_method, http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name="$service",deployment_environment_name="$environment",service_namespace=~"$namespace",host_name=~"$host"}[$__range])) > 0)

100 * (sum by (http_request_method, http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name="$service",deployment_environment_name="$environment",service_namespace=~"$namespace",host_name=~"$host",http_response_status_code=~"5.."}[$__range])) or 0 * sum by (http_request_method, http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name="$service",deployment_environment_name="$environment",service_namespace=~"$namespace",host_name=~"$host"}[$__range]))) / (sum by (http_request_method, http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name="$service",deployment_environment_name="$environment",service_namespace=~"$namespace",host_name=~"$host"}[$__range])) > 0)

panels.title: Database operations
panels.description: PostgreSQL client operations per second by pgx operation type. acquire is a connection checkout from the pool.

panels.title: Database errors
panels.description: Failed PostgreSQL client operations per second by operation type.

panels.title: Database p95 latency
panels.description: 95th percentile PostgreSQL client latency by operation type. A rising acquire line means the connection pool is exhausted and queries wait for a connection.

panels.title: Database health checks
panels.description: Hatchet's PostgreSQL checks, run every minute by the metrics collector: queries active for over 5 minutes, vacuums running for over 3 hours, and tables with over 50% dead tuples. Vacuum and bloat lines appear only while their check reports warn or alert. OTEL gauges keep the last value of each label set until the engine restarts, so a tenant, table, or SDK that stops reporting holds its last value. A warn line can therefore outlive the problem; confirm in PostgreSQL before acting.

defaults.noValue: No data yet: collected every minute when SERVER_OTEL_METRICS_ENABLED is on

panels.title: OLAP status-update backlog
panels.description: Rows waiting in the temporary tables that copy task and DAG status changes into the OLAP tables behind the Hatchet UI. Sustained growth means the OLAP controller is falling behind, so run statuses in the UI lag. Sampled every 5 minutes.

defaults.noValue: No data yet: collected every 5 min when SERVER_OTEL_METRICS_ENABLED is on

panels.title: Workflow runs yesterday
panels.description: Workflow runs from the previous UTC day by final status, recorded once a day at 00:05 UTC by the metrics collector.

panels.title: Most bloated tables
panels.description: Tables with over 50% dead tuples (and over 1000 dead tuples), worst first. Autovacuum should clear these; persistent entries need a manual VACUUM. OTEL gauges keep the last value of each label set until the engine restarts, so a tenant, table, or SDK that stops reporting holds its last value.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio of disk-heavy tables
panels.description: Heap-block cache hit ratio of the 20 tables with the most disk reads, lowest first. Counters are cumulative since PostgreSQL statistics were last reset, so old daily partitions read by retention cleanup or long-range UI queries often sit low. Hatchet flags tables below 95%; act when current partitions stay low, for example by raising shared_buffers. OTEL gauges keep the last value of each label set until the engine restarts, so a tenant, table, or SDK that stops reporting holds its last value.

defaults.noValue: No data yet: collected every minute when SERVER_OTEL_METRICS_ENABLED is on

panels.title: Time since autovacuum (active partitions)
panels.description: Time since autovacuum last ran on partitions that still receive writes: hash partitions plus the daily partitions dated on the time range's start or end day. Older daily partitions go idle after their day. Autovacuum runs after enough dead or inserted rows rather than on a schedule, and Hatchet creates partitions in advance, so a quiet partition can go days without one. Use this for context and act on Most bloated tables. Daily partitions are named in UTC while the date filter uses the browser's time zone. OTEL gauges keep the last value of each label set until the engine restarts, so a tenant, table, or SDK that stops reporting holds its last value.

defaults.noValue: No data yet: collected every minute when SERVER_OTEL_METRICS_ENABLED is on

targets.expr: sort_desc(topk(10, max by (table_name) (hatchet_db_last_autovacuum_seconds_since{service_name="$service",deployment_environment_name="$environment",service_namespace=~"$namespace",host_name=~"$host",table_name!~".*_[0-9]{8}"}) or max by (table_name) (hatchet_db_last_autovacuum_seconds_since{service_name="$service",deployment_environment_name="$environment",service_namespace=~"$namespace",host_name=~"$host",table_name=~".*_(${__from:date:YYYYMMDD}|${__to:date:YYYYMMDD})"})))

panels.title: Slowest engine operations (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile duration of internal engine spans (controllers, scheduler, queues) over the selected range, slowest first. Subscription spans, which last as long as the subscription, are excluded. Span metrics come from sampled traces (SERVER_OTEL_TRACE_ID_RATIO), so latency percentiles and rankings hold, but absolute counts are a fraction of real volume.

panels.title: Slowest database queries (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile duration of PostgreSQL client spans, named after Hatchet's sqlc queries, slowest first. pool.acquire is time spent waiting for a pooled connection. Span metrics come from sampled traces (SERVER_OTEL_TRACE_ID_RATIO), so latency percentiles and rankings hold, but absolute counts are a fraction of real volume.

panels.title: Database time by query
panels.description: Share of total PostgreSQL client time spent in each query over the selected range. Optimising the top entries cuts the most database load. Span metrics come from sampled traces (SERVER_OTEL_TRACE_ID_RATIO), so latency percentiles and rankings hold, but absolute counts are a fraction of real volume.

panels.title: Error spans by operation
panels.description: Sampled spans per second that ended with error status, by span name. HTTP 4xx responses also mark their server span as an error. Span metrics come from sampled traces (SERVER_OTEL_TRACE_ID_RATIO), so latency percentiles and rankings hold, but absolute counts are a fraction of real volume.

panels.title: Recent error spans
panels.description: Most recent sampled spans with error status. Click a Span ID to open the full trace. Only SERVER_OTEL_TRACE_ID_RATIO of traces are kept.

targets.query: { resource.service.name = "$service" && resource.deployment.environment.name = "$environment" && resource.service.namespace =~ "$namespace" && resource.host.name =~ "$host" && status = error } | select(name, statusMessage, span.rpc.method, span.rpc.response.status_code, span.http.route, span.http.response.status_code, span."hatchet.run/tenant.id") with (most_recent=true)

panels.title: Slow requests (> 500 ms)
panels.description: Most recent sampled gRPC and REST server spans slower than 500 ms. Streaming RPCs are excluded because their spans last as long as the stream. Click a Span ID to open the full trace.

targets.query: { resource.service.name = "$service" && resource.deployment.environment.name = "$environment" && resource.service.namespace =~ "$namespace" && resource.host.name =~ "$host" && kind = server && duration > 500ms && (span.rpc.method = nil || span.rpc.method !~ ".*/(Listen|ListenV2|SubscribeToWorkflowEvents|SubscribeToWorkflowRuns|DurableTask|ListenForDurableEvent|Subscribe)") } | select(name, span.rpc.method, span.rpc.response.status_code, span.http.route, span.http.response.status_code, span."hatchet.run/tenant.id") with (most_recent=true)

panels.title: CPU throttled periods
panels.description: Share of CFS scheduling periods in which the container hit its cpus limit. Sustained throttling slows scheduling and raises latency; raise the container's cpus limit.

panels.title: CPU throttled time
panels.description: Seconds per second that the container's threads spent throttled by its cpus limit.

panels.title: Memory limit hits
panels.description: Times the container's memory usage reached its mem_limit in each interval. Repeated hits precede OOM kills; raise the container's mem_limit.
